overlap_evidence: Bu and Che Mat (2026), DOI 10.13189/cea.2026.140514, compare three conceptual layouts within a 12 m² bedroom. PDF pp. 12–14 (§6.1–6.3, Fig. 10, Table 2) report approximately 5–5.5 m² of activity area for fixed furniture and approximately 8 m² when a wall bed is folded, described by the authors as roughly 60% improvement. The authors explicitly describe an analytical comparison, not measured performance in occupied dwellings (§3.3, §6.1, §7). Their time-based zoning is relevant to C2, but no shared-position schedule-constrained optimization algorithm, independent reachability validator or whole-dwelling FEA inversion is demonstrated in the checked methods/results. This is sufficient overlap with the broad C3 wording to activate the protocol stop; it does not establish that the entire proposed project has been done. These are the paper’s reported values, not results of our experiments. The full-text download URL, checksum, checked sections and evidence classification are recorded in fulltext_checks.json.
proposals: For reviewer consideration: add Bu & Che Mat as a C3 antecedent; MAFC-Driven Dynamic Layout Transformation System (10.1002/cav.70113) as a motion-coordination distinction for C2; and Mechanisms of Spatial Efficiency (10.55057/ijbtm.2025.7.6.13) as qualitative evidence on temporal adaptability. RESEARCH_PLAN has not been edited. Proposed narrower framing: quantify household-specific, time-weighted whole-dwelling functional equivalence on real plans with independently validated clearance and reachability, rather than claim the first numerical area benefit of transformable furniture. The reviewer must decide whether this distinction is sufficient.
limitations: Screening was deliberately interrupted when the explicit C3 stop rule was met; the pending majority has not been screened, and neither citation saturation nor absence of other overlaps can be claimed. OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429 responses. OpenAlex cursor continuation required a key (HTTP 401); a retry used documented public basic paging with 100 records per page, but repeated rate limiting left Q1 incomplete. Completed earlier responses were retained even when a later retry failed. All six Crossref keyword queries reached the configured 500-record cap and are relevance-ranked, not exhaustive Boolean searches. Semantic Scholar zero totals are retained as returned and do not demonstrate absence of literature. Crossref metadata was merged only where DOI or normalized title/year matched; unresolved field completion remains pending. OpenAlex applied language:en; other providers expose inconsistent language metadata, so the English-language restriction is not fully verified and non-English records remain unscreened. arXiv used HTTPS for the configured endpoint. The optional Chinese search was not run. One reviewer (Codex) made the explicit judgements. Full-text TLS validation succeeded using the operating system trust store after the Python client could not validate the publisher chain; no certificate checks were disabled.
